To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamics of generic viscoelastic systems can be described by a single equation of motion with the strain tensor and its time-derivative as the independent variables, and that the equation of motion is invariant under a certain symmetry group.
the dynamics of single component viscoelastic fluids can be described in the linear regime with a single relaxation parameter.
the viscoelasticity of a single-component system with a single relaxation is described by a foliation preserving differomorphism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the description of visco-elastic systems.
the description of the dynamics of viscoelastic systems in a unified way.
the description of the viscoelasticity in terms of a universal theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the foliation preserving difféomorphisms are a universal symmetry which determines the dynamics in the linear order of strains.
, the foliation preserving differomorphism symmetry is a natural and powerful tool to describe viscoelasticity in the first order in the strain.
, in the linear regime and in the absence of any external forces, a single-component visco-elastic fluid is characterized by the two parameters of the relaxation time and the shear modulus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics is described by a single equation for the trace of the velocity gradient.
a viscoelastic system is described by a set of coupled nonlinear equations of motions for a single scalar field, and the equations are universal for all single-component viscoelastics.
the foliation preserving differomorphisms are the most general class of diffeomorphims preserving the foliation of the phase space into elastic and fluid regions, with no additional constraints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the viscoelasticity can be described by a single scalar field.
the symmetry is sufficient to describe the dynamics of the system in the first order.
the dynamics of viscoelastic systems can be understood in a universal way.
